newsitem.title: MACEDONIA: Ex-Yugo successors agree asset division proposal. [CORRECTED 17:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Ex-Yugo successors agree asset division proposal. [CORRECTED 17:05 GMT]

text.p: The central bank governors of Bosnia, Slovenia, Croatia and Macedonia agreed on Monday to accept a proposal by the Bank for International Settlements in Basle for the division of assets of the National Bank of the former Yugoslavia.

The four governors met in Skopje, to discuss the division of joint gold and foreign currency reserves, totalling $600 million, held by the Basle-based bank. (Corrects location of meeting and nature of reserves)

The governors "agreed that the criteria proposed by the Bank for International Settlements are acceptable and provide a real chance for a speedier start of the succession of the assets of the former Yugoslavia in other spheres," the Macedonian Central Bank said.
The governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia did not attend the meeting despite being invited, but was sent a statement outlining the outcome.
Last week the four successor states were gridlocked in talks on the federal assets of former Yugoslavia at a meeting with international mediator Sir Arthur Watts in Brussels.

Since the United Nations lifted sanctions against Yugoslavia last year, Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Macedonia have acted together to block Belgrade's access to currency and other assets deposited abroad.
The property of ex-Yugoslavia is estimated at $70 billion in real estate and other property, foreign exchange and gold reserves.
The governors will next meet in Washington at the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.
